summary: First full review of this OUTCOME_AWARENESS/REACH ad set (running since 2026-05-16, ₹350/day). Near-zero CTR (~0.08%) is expected/normal for a reach-optimized objective, not a failure signal. Evidence it is doing what a reach campaign should: (1) cheapest CPM in the entire account by a wide margin - ₹1.98 CPM over the last 7 days vs ₹230 (Insta Engaged), ₹160 (WhatsApp), ₹91 (First Love); (2) daily frequency holds ~1.0-1.05x across 25 consecutive days (2026-07-11 to 2026-08-04) with no upward drift, meaning it keeps finding fresh people rather than re-hitting the same pool - no fatigue after ~3 months running; (3) targeting explicitly excludes the Insta Engaged 365D and Instagram Followers audiences (the account's warm remarketing pool) and instead uses 1%/1-2%/2-3% India lookalikes of Instagram Followers - a genuinely distinct, non-overlapping cold-prospecting audience, so it is not cannibalizing budget or delivery from the higher-performing warm campaigns; (4) spend share is small - ~6% of account 7-day spend (₹2,380 of ~₹39,381). No direct leads or purchases are attributed to it (expected - it is not optimized for those actions), only incidental trickle of messaging-conversation-starts (1-6/day) and rare add_to_cart/view_content events. No causal evidence it drives orders; also no evidence it is wasteful or harmful. Net read: cheap, non-cannibalizing top-of-funnel reach-building that other remarketing campaigns could in theory later monetize, unproven but low-cost.

subject: Meta platform intelligence - Advantage+ targeting-automation default shift (2025-2026)
summary: Researched Meta platform/algorithm changes for this month's review. Convergent third-party trade reporting (Social Media Today, socialsamosa.com, thekeyword.co - moderate-to-good credibility trade/industry press, not official Meta newsroom links which were not found) describes a sustained platform-wide shift through 2025-2026: detailed-targeting exclusions removed (Mar/Jun 2025), many detailed-interest categories consolidated or removed outright (Jun 2025 consolidation, deprecated interests stopped working Dec 2025, further categories removed Jan 15 2026), and as of Jan 2026 Meta reportedly made Advantage Detailed Targeting on by default for conversion and link-click campaigns - meaning manual interest inputs are treated as audience suggestions rather than hard constraints unless an advertiser explicitly disables audience expansion. Given this could materially affect a live, recently-modified ad set (First Love | Interest Stack, whose targeting fix was the subject of KL-2026-08-18-22 and confirmed live in KL-2026-08-20-160500), checked this empirically against K&A's own account rather than relying on the reporting alone: fresh GET on both relevant ad sets confirms neither is exposed to unintended default drift. First Love | Broad Advantage+ | India (52535906903180): targeting_automation.advantage_audience=1, an explicit deliberate choice (this ad set is meant to be broad). First Love | Interest Stack (52535906794980): targeting_automation.advantage_audience=0, explicitly disabled, so its 7 manually-added interests are being enforced as real constraints, not diluted into suggestions - the ad set's whole rationale (a targeting-differentiated pool distinct from Broad Advantage+, per KL-2026-08-18-22) is intact. Verdict: no live action needed today. Forward-looking process point worth carrying: since Meta's default for new campaigns/ad sets has shifted toward audience-expansion-on, media-buyer should keep explicitly setting targeting_automation.advantage_audience on every future ad set build (already current practice per both ad sets checked) rather than ever omitting the field and relying on whatever Meta's current default happens to be. Caveat on source quality: some corroborating sites for this topic are SEO-content-mill quality rather than primary trade journalism, and Meta's own claimed performance figures relayed by these sources (e.g. a 22.6% lower median cost-per-conversion without detailed-targeting exclusions) are Meta's self-reported testing, not independently verified - treat those specific numbers as directional context, not fact.
reasoning: Applying the standing test (does this matter for K&A's account) against a real, verifiable claim rather than accepting third-party reporting at face value - checked the actual live targeting objects instead of assuming exposure. Confirmed no gap exists, so this stays an observation/process note rather than escalating to a decision requiring a live change.

subject: India | Add to Cart 90D | Catalog DPA
summary: Independent read of the KL-2026-08-18-08 rollback tension: HOLD the new creative (2638573909894809), do not roll back to the old one (1761163224879104), and revise the judgment metric going forward. Fresh data at the 3-5 day check-in: CTR fell ~35% relative (pre-swap 7-day baseline 10.07% -> post-swap blended 6.60%, most recent 2 days 4.5-6.0%), which literally meets the KL-2026-08-18-08 rollback trigger as written ("CTR/link-click rate drops materially"). But that trigger was written before the funnel diagnosis in KL-2026-08-18-03/04 was fully internalized: the actual problem this swap was built to fix was never CTR - it was the view_content->add_to_cart drop-off (0.5% baseline, KL-2026-08-18-03), the stage above where the old checkout-friction theory had been looking. Post-swap, that exact metric roughly tripled to 1.53% (9/590). A plausible and more likely explanation than "the new creative is worse": the new copy (which foregrounds made-to-order/customization detail rather than a generic "still thinking it over" nudge) is self-selecting - fewer low-intent curiosity clicks, but a materially higher share of the people who do click going on to add to cart, which is precisely the mid-funnel fix intended. Purchases are still 0 both sides, but the post-swap sample (~3.5 real days, ~590 view_content, 9 add_to_cart) is too thin to read purchase absence as new information either way on a made-to-order luxury item with a consult/fitting-driven sales cycle - 3-5 days was never going to be long enough to see a purchase materialize even in a success case. Revised plan: (1) do not roll back; (2) extend the observation window to a full 7 days post-swap (through 2026-08-25) before any rollback/keep call, since that was always too short a window for the metric that actually matters (add_to_cart rate, and if reached, initiate_checkout/purchase); (3) re-frame the primary judgment metric for this specific creative test from CTR to view_content->add_to_cart rate and downstream checkout progression - CTR stays a secondary/sanity metric (still worth flagging if it falls further or if effective_status changes), not the deciding one, since the swap was never meant to be a CTR play; (4) if by 2026-08-25 add_to_cart rate has reverted back toward the ~0.5% baseline (i.e. the early tripling proves noise) or CTR has collapsed further with no offsetting funnel-quality gain, that is the real rollback trigger - not the literal CTR-drop text as originally written.
reasoning: Standing instruction (2026-08-18 Add to Cart Remarketing precedent) is explicit that an analyst finding a literal-trigger match is not the same as a strategist's independent read of what that trigger was actually meant to catch. Rolling back here on CTR alone would revert the one metric (view_content->add_to_cart) the swap was actually diagnosed and designed to fix, based on a trigger clause that predates and does not account for that diagnosis. No live account change implied by this decision (ad stays on its current, already-live creative) - nothing routed to media-buyer.
follow_up: Re-check at 7 full days post-swap (~2026-08-25): judge primarily on view_content->add_to_cart rate (does the ~1.5% hold or revert to ~0.5% baseline) and any initiate_checkout/purchase movement; CTR as secondary sanity check only. If add_to_cart rate reverts to baseline or CTR collapses further with no funnel-quality offset, that is the real rollback trigger - revert to creative 1761163224879104 at that point, not before.

reasoning: Per docs/architecture.md section 3c: commercial outcomes (orders, revenue) carry the actual weight here, not CTR or engagement, and this findings evidence is entirely revenue-based across two independent time windows, which is why it clears the bar for action while the weaker single-proxy Punjab and Karnataka pattern does not yet. Chose a geographic ad-set test over a larger reallocation or dedicated campaign specifically because none of the existing prospecting ad sets are geo-targeted at all right now, so isolating the variable is the more honest first step than assuming the answer and reallocating budget on an unconfirmed causal read.
follow_up: Route to media-buyer: prepare a build plan (paused first) for First Love | Maharashtra-Mumbai Geo Test | India under campaign 52535906524580, Rs150 per day net-new, reusing existing First Love creative to start. subject: India | Add to Cart 90D audience overlap check (ad set 52542179758780 DPA vs ad set 52547119740980 WhatsApp Consult Test)
summary: Verified the cannibalization theory raised today re: ad set 1 (52542179758780, DPA, campaign 52542179696580) vs ad set 2 (52547119740980, WhatsApp Consult Test, campaign 6858349204776) sharing custom audience 'Add to Cart 90 D' (id 6693713537576). VERDICT: the specific mechanism proposed (ad set 2 winning delivery share and shrinking ad set 1's reach) is CONTRADICTED by direct measurement, not confirmed. 1) Pulled ad set 1 / ad 52542179867180 daily reach+impressions 2026-08-17 through 2026-08-24 (GET .../insights?time_increment=1): reach 1100 -> 1575 -> 1652 -> 5386 -> 4426 -> 5706 -> 10771 -> 7733 (08-17 through 08-24). Ad set 1's own reach GREW substantially (~7-10x, peaking 08-23) over the exact same window ad set 2's reach grew 13x (609->7664 per the prior correlational check) - it did not decline or even plateau. This directly weakens the 'competing for the same delivery pool shrunk ad set 1's reach' theory as literally framed - both ad sets' reach grew together, which reads more like a shared account/campaign-level delivery ramp than one ad set winning auctions at the other's direct expense. 2) No Meta Marketing API tooling found to confirm overlap more directly for these two specific ad sets: tried /audience_overlap and /overlap edges on both the ad account and the custom audience object - both return 'Unknown path components' (code 2500, not supported via Graph API, Audience Overlap is a Business Manager UI-only tool with no public API equivalent found). Tried act_.../reachestimate for the shared audience's targeting spec - returned users_lower_bound/upper_bound both -1 (unusable/unavailable for this spec). Stating this plainly per instructions rather than approximating: there is no API-confirmable overlap metric available, only the indirect reach-timing correlation already on record. 3) NEW finding relevant to alternative explanations: pulled the custom audience object directly (GET 6693713537576?fields=approximate_count_lower_bound,approximate_count_upper_bound) - the named audience 'Add to Cart 90 D' has an approximate size of only ~20 people (lower_bound=upper_bound=20). Both ad sets' targeting has targeting_automation.advantage_audience=1 (Advantage Detailed Targeting / audience expansion) enabled - confirmed via GET on both ad set objects. Since actual daily reach on both ad sets (thousands) vastly exceeds the ~20-person named audience, essentially all real delivery on both ad sets is coming from Meta's algorithmic expansion beyond the literal list, using the tiny seed + India geo + 18-65 age as signal, not from the named audience membership itself. This reframes the 'same audience' framing: the two ad sets share an expansion SEED and geo, not a fixed delivery pool, so a strict membership-overlap check would not be meaningful even if the tooling existed - the real question is whether Meta's expansion algorithm is drawing overlapping expanded pools for both, which cannot be confirmed or denied with available tooling. 4) Ruled out frequency fatigue on ad set 1 itself: frequency stayed flat and low (1.12-1.30) across the entire window, nowhere near fatigue territory - not a contributing factor. 5) Pulled raw add_to_cart action counts alongside link_click for the same window to sanity-check the rate collapse already on record (not just a denominator artifact): link_click grew across the window (155->160->181->240->179->265->431->373) while add_to_cart count fell to 2 (08-22), 1 (08-23), 0 (08-24) - confirms the collapse is real in absolute terms, not a rate-denominator illusion: rising top-of-funnel traffic with vanishing bottom-of-funnel action is more characteristic of a landing/catalog/creative-stage break than of simple reach-share loss. This is consistent with (does not contradict) the copy-quality theory already on record in KL-2026-08-25-081500, and does not itself confirm or deny the DPA catalog concern flagged separately in KL-2026-08-18-03. Seasonality: no data pulled either way, not assessed here. OVERALL: the specific reach-competition hypothesis as stated is CONTRADICTED (ad set 1's reach grew, not declined). A subtler shared-expansion-pool dilution mechanism (same tiny seed + advantage_audience on both) remains structurally plausible given the ~20-person seed size but is NOT confirmed or denied by any available tool - genuinely inconclusive on that narrower point, not a forced conclusion either way. Net: this finding should reduce confidence that audience competition was a primary driver of ad set 1's add_to_cart collapse, and leaves the copy-quality/catalog explanations already on record as the better-supported ones pending further evidence.
reasoning: Task explicitly required verifying the correlation rather than accepting it at face value - the direct test (did ad set 1's reach decline concurrently) is the cleanest falsifiable check available and it came back negative for the theory as literally framed. Reporting that plainly rather than reframing the ask post-hoc to fit a confirmed-cannibalization narrative. The ~20-person seed audience + advantage_audience-on-both finding was not asked for directly but is material context for anyone revisiting this theory later, so logging it alongside rather than only answering the literal reach-decline question.

subject: diagnostic-methodology-shared-audience-check
summary: Before diagnosing a performance decline as a creative/copy/targeting problem, check whether any other active ad set shares the same custom audience (or targeting spec) as the one under review, and explicitly rule out or account for competition/interaction between them before concluding the change under review (not the shared audience) is the cause.
reasoning: Today's rollback verdict (KL-2026-08-25-081500) diagnosed the DPA ad's declining add_to_cart rate as a creative-copy problem without checking that a second active ad set (Whatsapp Consult Test, KL-2026-08-24-172200's subject) targets the identical custom audience (6693713537576) and had just scaled reach ~13x and received a budget increase in the same window. The theory turned out NOT to hold on direct evidence (performance-analyst's reach comparison in KL-2026-08-25-053441 showed the DPA ad set's own reach grew alongside the other's, not declined, and campaign-strategist's independent read in KL-2026-08-25-090800 confirmed the copy-quality diagnosis instead) - but the check should have been run as a matter of course, not only after a human flagged the gap after the fact. The absence of a competing cause is only established once it's actually checked, not assumed by default. This generalizes beyond this one pair of ad sets: any time two or more active ad sets/campaigns share a custom audience, lookalike source, or targeting spec, and one of them shows a performance shift, the shared-audience relationship is a first-class candidate explanation to test directly (e.g. via each object's own reach/impressions trend over the same window) before attributing the shift solely to a creative, copy, or on-object targeting change.
follow_up: performance-analyst and campaign-strategist: when investigating a performance decline/shift on any ad set/campaign, check (via a quick grep for the shared audience/lookalike/targeting-spec id across other active ad sets, plus each object's own delivery-metric trend over the same window) whether another active ad set shares the same audience before concluding the decline is caused by the change under review alone. If no other ad set shares the audience, note that explicitly as a ruled-out check rather than silently skipping it.

Diagnosis: this is not early variance still worth waiting out - it is a delivery-starvation problem, not a CTR problem, and the literal stop-rule (KL-2026-08-27-015920) cannot and structurally will not trigger under current conditions. The CTR observed on the 99 impressions this ad has received (2.02%) is actually ABOVE the sibling ad's CTR (1.60%), so there is no evidence people who see the ad are unpersuaded by it - the problem is that Meta's ad-level delivery optimization within the shared ad set is almost entirely routing the ad set's ~Rs350/day budget and auction opportunities to the stronger-predicted sibling (52535907844980: Rs570.92/8863 impressions over the same 3-day window vs this ad's Rs25.14/99 impressions, nearly all on day one). Because the stop-rule's CTR-comparison leg requires ~1000 impressions to evaluate, and this delivery pattern is itself what is preventing those impressions from ever accumulating, waiting longer under the current shared-budget structure is not a neutral holding pattern - it is very likely to just repeat the same near-zero-delivery result indefinitely, per Metas well-documented tendency to concentrate ad-set budget on whichever ad has the strongest early predicted performance signal once one ad pulls ahead. This is not a one-off: the identical Blush Pink Lehenga video asset already showed the same negligible-delivery pattern in a structurally different context (Broad Advantage+, ad 52547120474380, 1 messaging conversation across 5 days, per KL-2026-08-26-072044), where the ad set as a whole was healthy. Two independent occurrences of negligible delivery for this exact asset, across two different audiences/targeting mechanisms (manual interest-stack vs Advantage+ automatic), shifts the most likely explanation from audience-fit toward the asset itself being down-weighted by Metas delivery system regardless of audience - plausibly a weak early engagement/watch-time signal on the video itself (hook, thumbnail, first few seconds), which is a creative question, not a targeting question. This is the exact risk flagged as worth watching at approval time (KL-2026-08-27-015554s caveat) and, in substance if not in the letter of the written rule, has now materialized. DISPOSITION: treat as materialized, not as unresolved variance. PROPOSED NEXT MOVE (fully specified, not executed - routing to media-buyer for validation and an execution plan per todays no-live-write boundary): pause ad 52548730700780 (status ACTIVE -> PAUSED), a single status-only field change with no budget or targeting impact - ad set 52535906794980 daily_budget stays at Rs350/day unchanged, reverting to the single-active-ad state it was in before this activation, sibling ad 52535907844980 continues unaffected. Total committed spend on the paused ad so far is only Rs25.14, so the financial stakes of this call are minimal either way; the reason to act now rather than wait is that continuing to hold under the current shared-budget structure produces no new information and no meaningful test of the creative, not that it is burning meaningful money. subject: First Love | A Lehenga Built Like a Corset | Interest Stack (ad 52548730700780, video_id 1558544592573452) - hook/thumbnail/first-3-seconds diagnostic review, requested per KL-2026-08-29-015310
summary: Diagnostic review requested by campaign-strategist (KL-2026-08-29-015310) after the same video asset showed a near-zero-delivery pattern twice: Broad Advantage+ ad 52547120474380 (1 messaging conversation across 5 days, KL-2026-08-26-072044) and Interest Stack ad 52548730700780 (99 impressions day one, zero impressions for two full days after, paused 2026-08-29 per KL-2026-08-29-020500/021500). LIMITATION STATED UP FRONT: this role has no video-viewing tool. This diagnosis is built from the written creative brief/build record, comparative learning-log evidence, and craft knowledge of what drives early watch-time/thruplay prediction for paid video delivery - not from watching the footage. KEY FINDING (isolates the variable): the video_id (1558544592573452) and the cover-frame thumbnail (image_hash 5e3cf0ec0bc69a4b5247fc1f116abec0) are IDENTICAL, byte-for-byte reused, across both failed ads. Confirmed via build records: Broad Advantage+ ad 52547120474380 was built 2026-08-18 (KL-2026-08-18-15/18) with headline The Softest Version of Bold and its own primary text; Interest Stack ad 52548730700780 was built 2026-08-24 (KL-2026-08-24-010600/120019) explicitly reusing the same video_id and the same image_hash - the media-buyer plan states this directly: reusing the SAME image_hash values already validated and live on the existing Broad Advantage+ ads for these exact videos, no new image upload needed. So headline, primary text, CTA framing, audience/targeting mechanism (manual interest-stack vs Advantage+ broad), and ad set all differed between the two failures - only the video and thumbnail stayed constant. That is strong evidence the constant, not the variables, is the cause. RULED OUT as primary cause: (1) targeting/audience - failed under two structurally different mechanisms already (per KL-2026-08-29-015310's own logic, reaffirmed here); (2) copy/CTA - different headline and body text both times, same failure pattern, and on the small sample that DID see the Interest Stack ad, CTR was healthy and actually above the sibling ad's (2.02% vs 1.60%, per KL-2026-08-29-020500) - people who see it are not obviously unpersuaded, so this reads as a pre-click delivery-prediction problem (Meta not choosing to serve it), not a post-click persuasion problem; (3) compliance/disapproval - both ads passed review cleanly with empty issues_info both times, confirmed fresh both instances. MOST LIKELY EXPLANATION, in order, given the above: (a) the cover-frame thumbnail was never a deliberate choice - build mechanism both times was GET /{video-id}/thumbnails then POST .../adimages, i.e. picking from Metas auto-generated candidate frames, not hand-selecting or designing a frame for stopping power. It was set once (2026-08-18) and then carried forward unchanged and untested as an independent variable through a second, structurally different ad. (b) the source footage itself (organic Instagram Reel Db5wi_BsHTC, posted 2026-08-11, sourced by social-community-manager per KL-2026-08-18-05, uploaded directly as an ad video with no re-cut) was originally shot/edited for an organic-follower audience, where a slower reveal pattern (establish mood, then reveal the full look) is a normal and often effective organic pacing choice - but paid cold/interest delivery is evaluated by Metas system on very early watch-time signal (effectively the first 1-3 seconds), where a slow atmospheric open competes poorly against faster-hooking content in the same auction. NOTABLE GAP BETWEEN BRIEF AND EXECUTION: the second creative brief for this exact asset (KL-2026-08-21-015443, Variant 1) explicitly specified a materially different, faster-hooking cut - open tight on the corset bodice/structural seam line first, establishing structure before revealing the skirt, then cut to a slow full-silhouette reveal, close inserts on waist seam/lacing, warm intimate bridal lighting - written specifically to lead with the structural hook. But the actual build (KL-2026-08-24-010600/120019) never produced a new edit against that direction; it reused the identical existing video_id and thumbnail from the first build and layered only new title/message text on top. So the second failure is not evidence that a properly re-cut hook would also fail - a re-cut hook, as already specified in writing, was never actually tried. This is the concrete, actionable gap: the fix that was already designed on paper was never executed against the video itself.
reasoning: Weighted the two-failures-same-constant pattern (video_id + thumbnail identical, everything else different) as the strongest available evidence given no direct video-viewing access - this is the same reasoning standard campaign-strategist used to move from audience-fit to asset-fit (KL-2026-08-29-015310), extended one level further to isolate which part of the asset (thumbnail vs footage vs copy) is implicated, using build records rather than assumption. Cross-checked recipe 6 (best_practice) and recipe 4 (creative/product tags) per standing instruction before writing this - found no prior best_practice or outcome entries specifically about hook/thumbnail/watch-time performance for this account, so this diagnosis has no directly comparable precedent to weigh against and relies on general video-ads craft knowledge plus the specific comparative evidence in this account's own log; flagged explicitly rather than overstating certainty (confidence: medium, not high).
follow_up: GATE for any future re-test decision (owned by campaign-strategist, not this entry - this entry deliberately does not propose a re-test): do not re-test video_id 1558544592573452 / image_hash 5e3cf0ec0bc69a4b5247fc1f116abec0 unchanged a third time in any ad set - two clean failures across different copy and different targeting mechanisms have already answered whether that exact pairing performs. Before any future re-test: (1) produce a genuinely new edit (new video_id) of the Db5wi_BsHTC footage, or new footage entirely, actually executing the recut direction already specified in KL-2026-08-21-015443 but never built - open on the corset bodice/structural seam line within the first 1-2 seconds rather than a slower atmospheric build, cut promptly to the full-silhouette reveal; (2) generate 3-4 deliberately hand-picked candidate cover-frame thumbnails rather than reusing a Meta-auto-suggested frame, prioritizing an unblurred frame that reads the garments structure/color clearly, ideally with the models face/expression visible. If a recut is not feasible, this specific raw footage should be treated as not a fixable variable for paid cold/interest delivery and retired from future paid re-tests - fine to keep as organic content only, where it was originally sourced and presumably performs adequately.

subject: _happybrar UGC ad-set test - creative brief (reel selection, copy, crediting, test structure)
summary: Creative brief for the new _happybrar UGC ad-set test authorized in KL-2026-08-31-020800. FIRST-EVER UGC-BASED PAID AD FOR THIS ACCOUNT: checked the full learning-log UGC history (KL-2026-08-07-07 rjxartistry/kinjalshuklabhanushali declined; KL-2026-08-19/20 taran_smiles held then never actually launched as an ad; ayeshameht/richa_thakkar26/others rejected or no-action) -- every prior UGC item was declined, held, or FYI-only. No UGC content has ever actually run as a paid K&A ad before this. This is a genuine first, not an established pattern. REEL SELECTION: launch with ONE reel only -- 18125126245694535 (428 likes/8 comments, 'my biggest cheerleader', strongest engagement of the three, posted 2026-08-24) -- not all three together. Rationale: guardrail 11 (stagger near-identical creative activation) applies directly -- all three reels are the same real bride/reception content, near-identical in subject and format, so running them simultaneously in one small test ad set would blur the read on whether the UGC ANGLE ITSELF works (this account's actual open question, being tested for the first time) versus which of three similar clips performs best (a second-order question not worth asking yet). Hold 17896211106596684 (177 likes) as the staggered follow-up creative -- add it only several days after launch and only if the initial read is positive, never simultaneously. Hold 17879113575522704 (98 likes, weakest of the three) in reserve, not scheduled. COPY/FRAMING APPROACH: light-touch wrap, not a rewrite. The reel's own footage, her own voice, and her own caption framing stay untouched -- K&A's copy wraps around it only as the Primary Text/headline/CTA in Ads Manager, functioning as a testimonial frame, not a re-edited ad script. Over-polishing or re-scripting UGC kills the exact authenticity advantage it has over the account's all-studio-shot library, so no voiceover replacement, no re-cut, no studio-style text overlays baked into the video itself. FINAL COPY -- Headline: 'Real Brides, Real K&A'. Primary text: "'My biggest cheerleader.' -- that's how one real K&A bride captioned her reception moment, and we couldn't put it better. This is her look, her day, unedited: structured, hand-embellished, unmistakably K&A. If you're planning your own reception or wedding look, we'd love to help you find yours. Enquire for pricing and customization, or book a video consult with our team. Video credit: @_happybrar | Styling & fabric: @silkenthreads_canada". CTA button: 'Send Message' (WhatsApp/DM click-to-message, matching the account's lead-gen-first funnel, not a direct 'Shop Now'). Optional secondary line if a lead form is used instead: 'Book a virtual or in-studio consult -- worldwide shipping, made-to-order.' CREDITING DECISION: credit @_happybrar (the creator) and @silkenthreads_canada (the fabric/styling vendor she named in her own caption) by handle directly in the ad's Primary Text, as a courtesy per campaign-strategist's explicit question in KL-2026-08-31-020800's follow_up -- not legally required post-KL-2026-08-26-130000, but costs nothing and is consistent with brand voice/goodwill. NOTE: 'karishmaashita' in her outfit-credit tag is K&A's OWN Instagram handle (see brand-brief.md), not a third-party vendor -- no separate credit owed there, only silkenthreads_canada is external. SEPARATE FLAG for media-buyer: crediting here means a text mention in ad copy, not routing this through Meta's native Partnership Ads / branded-content tagging tool -- that tool has its own creator-side acceptance step, a distinct platform mechanism from the general repost-permission policy KL-2026-08-26-130000 addressed. Recommend building this as an owned/uploaded creative asset with a text credit, not attempting a Partnership Ads flow, unless media-buyer knows otherwise. PROPOSED TEST STRUCTURE (for campaign-strategist/media-buyer to validate -- outside creative-copywriter's normal scope but asked for explicitly this cycle): new ad set under the existing 'Insta Engaged and Followers Remarketing' campaign (India engaged/follower audience), not a new campaign (insufficient volume/evidence yet, matching KL-2026-08-31-020800's own reasoning) and not First Love/Broad Advantage+ cold prospecting. Reasoning: authentic testimonial-style UGC earns its keep by lowering perceived risk on a high-ticket considered purchase for people who already know the brand and are closer to a decision -- a warm/engaged audience is the cleaner first test of whether the UGC ANGLE lifts performance, versus a cold audience where the account's existing highly-produced studio content already does the scroll-stopping job, which would confound the read. Budget: TBD by media-buyer within the standing daily ceiling, net-new and modest given this is an unproven angle. STOP-RULE: run a minimum 7-14 day window (matching this account's existing 1-2 week reassessment bar, see KL-2026-08-20-170500) or until a minimum meaningful spend is reached, whichever is later -- don't judge on a thinner sample. Compare CTR and cost-per-result against the sibling studio-creative ad set(s) in the same campaign over the same window, and check Stitchflow for actual enquiry quality, not Meta metrics alone. EXPAND if cost-per-result is at or below the studio-creative baseline, or CTR is notably higher: stagger in reel 17896211106596684 next, and revisit whether a dedicated UGC/real-bride campaign is worth building. KILL/HOLD the angle (keep studio creative as primary, don't add the third reel) if cost-per-result is meaningfully worse (e.g. >50% higher) or CTR is below baseline after the minimum window. Log the eventual result as a type:outcome entry linked to this one either way, so this doesn't get silently re-litigated without a data trail.
reasoning: UGC best practice (authenticity over polish) argues for minimal K&A intervention in the footage itself; guardrail 11 argues against activating near-identical creative simultaneously; the account's stated funnel reality (lead-gen first, no bare 'Shop Now') and brand voice rules (no discount/urgency language) shaped the copy; warm-audience placement follows from what social proof actually does for a considered purchase, distinct from a cold-prospecting scroll-stop job the existing studio library already performs. Explicitly verified via full log grep that this is the account's first real UGC-based paid ad, not an established pattern, since every prior UGC item on record was declined, held, or FYI-only with no completed ad build.
evidence: Reel engagement: 18125126245694535 (428 likes/8 comments, 2026-08-24, selected), 17896211106596684 (177 likes, staggered follow-up), 17879113575522704 (98 likes, reserve). Full learning-log UGC-history grep confirms no prior UGC content has ever run as a completed paid ad on this account.
follow_up: media-buyer to validate the exact build (which ad set/campaign, budget within ceiling, owned-asset upload vs any Partnership Ads mechanics) and prepare the execution plan for user approval; performance-analyst to track CTR/cost-per-result vs. sibling studio-creative ad set(s) and Stitchflow enquiry quality against the stated stop-rule window; log the eventual outcome as type:outcome linked to this entry.
